feature: Auto-login after set-password via signup-exchange token (Git #636, Epic: A. Core Assessment Product)
notes: Git #1052 — the MINT step (POST /public/flow/set-password) remains unreachable by the harness: it requires a real Stripe-paid checkout session (and, for a first-time buyer, the earlier Microsoft admin-consent OAuth callback that provisions the users row) — the same architectural wall #987's money-path-e2e.json carves out. But that wall belongs to set-password, not to /auth/signup-exchange itself, which has zero dependency on Stripe or OAuth. The EXCHANGE endpoint's real happy path is therefore genuinely covered below via a dev-only testbed seed (POST /admin/testbed/seed-signup-token, Git #1052, same requireDevOrigin + requireAdminOrIngestToken pattern as #986's admin-testbed.ts routes) rather than fabricated — a real signupExchangeTokensTable row is inserted for the designated testbed Assessment account, then genuinely exchanged for a real session, and a second exchange with the same token is asserted to hit the real single-use guard. The two original guard-path tests below (missing/bogus token) are unchanged and still cover the endpoint's negative-path shape.
shaneapp://runTest couriers to the DEPLOYED BuildConsole/api-server instance, not this session's uncommitted worktree code — see the buildconsole-runtest memory.

apiTests.name: POST /auth/signup-exchange with no token body — 400, same shape as print-exchange's own guard
POST /auth/signup-exchange with a bogus/never-issued token — 401, never a session

expect.value: Invalid, expired, or already-used signup token

apiTests.name: HAPPY-PATH SETUP — log in as the designated testbed Assessment account to resolve its real users.id
HAPPY-PATH SEED — Git #1052 dev-only testbed route mints a real, single-use signupExchangeTokensTable row for that user
HAPPY-PATH EXCHANGE — POST /auth/signup-exchange with the seeded token — 200, real session-issuing contract (accessToken/refreshToken/refreshExpiresAt/user)
HAPPY-PATH SINGLE-USE — replaying the SAME seeded token — 401, proving the token was actually consumed, not just returned

expect.value: Invalid, expired, or already-used signup token
